meta.title: Real-time decoding with fast feedback

paper.authors: L. Caune, L. Skoric, N. S. Blunt et al. (Riverlane, Rigetti)
paper.title: Demonstrating real-time and low-latency quantum error correction with superconducting qubits

meta.summary: A stability experiment on 8 qubits of Rigetti's Ankaa-2, decoded in real time by a Collision Clustering decoder on an FPGA of the control system, and a fast-feedback test in which the decoded result conditions a pulse 9.6 µs after the last readout.
meta.program: The circuits the authors executed (their Zenodo record of Quil and sequencer programs, with the Stim circuits they generate): the stability-8 patch with 5 and 25 decoding rounds, and the fast-feedback run with 9 measurement rounds and its own four-CZ-layer schedule. After the circuit, the `decode_syndrome` system call on the decoder core; in the fast-feedback run, an RX(π) on Q50 conditioned on the decoder's logical-flip bit, as the paper's test does.
meta.twin: The 8 qubits on the Ankaa-2 lattice, every layer as long as its longest pulse in the executed programs: CZ per pair (68–176 ns), 40 ns RX, readout pulse and ring-down per qubit (up to 1312 ns). Rigetti's control system (a Kintex-7 card cage, the decoder on a sequencer FPGA at 156.25 MHz) is replaced by one RISC-Q board at 500 MHz: one core per qubit, a frame core and the decoder core running the compiled union-find decoder (the paper's decoder "achieves the same logical fidelities as the Union Find algorithm").
findings: Every operation of all three circuits ran inside its window: 11.24 µs for 5 decoding rounds, 44.84 µs for 25, and 16.96 µs for the fast-feedback run.

The fast-feedback loop on the twin: the bits reach the decoder 0.50 µs after the last readout window (Rigetti: 1.4 µs), the decode takes 47.1 µs (Rigetti's FPGA: 6.5 µs), and the conditioned pulse starts 0.48 µs after the result. The response is 48.1 µs against the paper's 9.6 µs. Moving bits on the RISC-Q board is about four times faster than Rigetti's path; decoding in firmware on one RISC-Q core is about seven times slower than their FPGA decoder.

The compiled decoder was run instruction by instruction on RISC-Q's own RTL in Verilator on 12 shots of the fast-feedback circuit: all 132,446 instructions commit on the same cycle as in the Lean model, and the 12 corrections and decode times (21,667–63,193 cycles) are the same.

The decode grows with the rounds decoded: 72.3 µs for 5 rounds and 285.8 µs for 25 in the run; over 400 noisy shots of 25 rounds, a median of 202 µs and at worst 537 µs. A real-time decoder for long experiments needs a sliding window: the calibration gives the compiler a 4-round window at d = 5.

Logical errors under the device-informed model: 24.6% for 5 rounds (paper 28.1%) and 6.3% for 25 (paper 20.5%). The model holds the medians of the paper's gate and readout errors and the qubits' T1 and T2; at 25 rounds the experiment is far worse than this model, which has no leakage and no drift.
The compiled decoder corrects like PyMatching on 83–94% of noisy shots, and its logical error is within a few tenths of a percent of PyMatching's at every round count.
limits: The noise is a device-informed model from the medians in the paper's Methods; per-qubit errors, leakage and crosstalk are not modeled.
The twin's decoder is union-find in firmware, not the paper's Collision Clustering on an FPGA: its decode time is the twin's, not Rigetti's.
No resets: as on the device, a 250 µs wait between shots (not simulated).

device.title: Rigetti Ankaa-2, the 8 qubits of the stability-8 patch
device.basis: The circuits are the authors' own (Zenodo, the executed programs and their Stim circuits), qubit for qubit, on the Ankaa-2 lattice positions. Every layer lasts its longest pulse as the programs give it: CZ per pair, readout and ring-down per qubit. Rigetti's control system (Kintex-7 card cage, a Collision Clustering decoder on a sequencer FPGA at 156.25 MHz) is replaced by QuantumOS's RISC-Q model: one core per qubit and a decoder core running the compiled union-find decoder (the paper's decoder "achieves the same logical fidelities as the Union Find algorithm").

noise.note: Device-informed (the agent's model from the medians in the paper's Methods, arXiv v1): depolarizing CZ 5/4·(1 − 97.3%), RX(π/2) 3/2·(1 − 99.86%), readout as a classical flip of the reported bit with 1 − 93.3% (no reset, so not an X error), and T1 = 13.2 µs, T2 = 10.6 µs Pauli-twirled damping of every idle qubit over each layer's time.

exact_as_published: Qubits, roles and checks (Methods; Fig. 1(b), 2(a)); Q44 unused.

Gate sequence of circuit-stability-r{5,9,25}.stim: identical gate DAG, detectors and observable to the authors' Zenodo Stim circuits main_meas06/10/26 and to the executed Quil programs (layers (e)-(j) of Fig. 2: RX(-pi/2) data, RX(+pi/2) ancillas, CZ layer g, CZ layer h, RX(-pi/2) ancillas, MEASURE; final round RX(-pi/2) on all 8, ancilla then data readout).
Detectors (m_r xor m_(r-2); m_2 alone) and observable (parity of the four first-round ancilla outcomes) are the authors' own, read from Zenodo; verified deterministic.
No resets; ancillas measured mid-circuit and re-used.
circuit-feedback-n9.stim: identical to the authors' ff_meas09.stim (fast-feedback schedule)
All pulse durations (CZ, RX, readout, ring-down) are the stored DEFCAL/DELAY values.
reconstructed_or_changed: QUBIT_COORDS: Ankaa-2 lattice positions (col = q mod 7, row = q div 7) instead of the authors' rotated coordinates; DETECTOR coordinates likewise (col, row, decoding round).
Stim qubit index -> device qubit map: derived (measured-qubit lists stored per run vs the Stim M order; consistent with CZ adjacency and the rotated coordinates), not stated in text.
Dropped the published files' trailing 'SQRT_X ...; S ...' after the last measurement (no effect on any record; absent from the executed programs).
TICK placement: one TICK per FENCE-separated hardware layer of the program; the final data readout is a separate layer in the LEP program but simultaneous in the fast-feedback program.

Final data readout (exact as executed, interpretation ours): the data were prepared with RX(-pi/2) (LEP) / RX(+pi/2) (feedback) and are read out after the same rotation, i.e. each data qubit is measured in the Y basis it was prepared in. The parity of the four data bits is then deterministic (it is the weight-4 Y37 Y43 Y45 Y51 operator, which commutes with all four ZZ checks), but neither the authors' detectors nor their observable use it, and neither do ours.
The meaning of R in file names: R = decoding rounds (paper's x-axis), measurement rounds = R + 1.
Noise models in verify.py are ours (the SI model of the paper plus a device-informed and a defect-rate-matched variant); they are sanity checks, not a reproduction of the device.

decoder.quote: The decoder we use is an FPGA implementation of a Collision Clustering decoder, which achieves the same logical fidelities as the Union Find algorithm. Modifications were made to the FPGA decoder of Ref. [barber] to allow for decoding the stability experiment and syndrome extraction circuits without mid-circuit reset operations.
decoder.section: Integrating an FPGA decoder in the Ankaa-2 control system
decoder.graph_quote: The FPGA decoder decoding graph does not use edge weights.

real_time.quote: The stabilizer measurement outcomes are automatically passed to the decoder during circuit execution. Once the decoder receives the allocated number of measurements, the measurements are converted to a syndrome and decoding is performed. The decoded result, along with data storing the decoder speed and status, is written to allocated registers.
real_time.section: Integrating an FPGA decoder in the Ankaa-2 control system
real_time.note: Decoding starts after the last round (batch decode of the whole experiment), not as a streaming decoder: 'To support this, the FPGA decoder should be updated to be a streaming decoder' (Conclusion).

bus.value: 32-bit WISHBONE via sequencer I/O ports, 250 MHz -> 156.25 MHz clock crossing
bus.quote: We used a version of the FPGA decoder featuring a 32-bit WISHBONE interface for communication.

decoder_location.quote: we selected the FPGA design with the lowest resource utilization, the gate drive card design, which is responsible for generating microwave pulses to enact single-qubit gates
decoder_location.zenodo: Q50 charge-drive sequencer (Transmon-50_charge_tx), instrument tsunami08 card 8

offline_decoders.quote: We use implementations in PyMatching 2 and BeliefMatching for the MWPM and belief-matching decoders, respectively. We use Stim to set up the circuits that represent our experiments and use these circuits to initialise the software decoders.

offline_noise_model.quote: Depolarisation of both qubits after each two-qubit gate with probability p. Depolarisation of each idle qubit and after each single-qubit gate, including measurement and reset operations, with probability p/10. Measurement flip with probability p.
offline_noise_model.p_quote: We decided to use p=0.03 based on the median two qubit gate fidelities on Ankaa-2.

decoder_registers_from_program.note: names/addresses from the executed assembly; meanings beyond the comments are our reading
decoder_registers_from_program.0x1080: control: write 0x1 reset, 0x4 start decoding (read-modify-write, mask 0xffffff00)
decoder_registers_from_program.0x1090: DACTLR: experiment config 0x0{d}02026c, d = decoding rounds (mask 0x83)
decoder_registers_from_program.0x1098: DASR: 'homology' = decoded logical flip (LSB used for the branch)
